components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 16px; background: #67e8f9; color: #020617; font: 600 14px 'Sarasa Term TC SemiBold', Menlo, monospace; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #a5f3fc; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(103 232 249 / 0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Ghost Button

components.name: Text Field

narrative.overview:
Noverterm is a dark, cool workspace where every piece of chrome is a thin sheet of frosted glass laid over a near-black blue gradient, and the terminal itself is the one opaque, solid surface. The glass is how the app says "light": panels are translucent white at single-digit opacity, edged by a one-pixel frost border, so the structure reads without adding visual weight.

Restraint governs the glass. Hierarchy comes from borders and tonal steps in white opacity, not from lift. Signal Cyan is the only accent with a voice: it marks the active tab, the primary action, the focused field. Everything else is slate text on midnight. Status lights (green, amber, red dots) are the only other color, and they carry information, never decoration.

The whole interface is set in one monospaced face, Sarasa Term, so chrome and terminal share a single typographic voice. Density is moderate: 14px text, 44px fields and top bar, generous rounding that softens the monospace grid.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black blue canvas with faint cyan and blue radial glows at the edges.
Translucent panels (white 4–10%) with a one-pixel white 8–10% border.
One accent, Signal Cyan, reserved for active and primary states.
A single monospace typeface for every text role.
Large, soft radii: 16px controls, ~22px cards, 28–32px panels and dialogs.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan means "active, focused, or primary". Never use it for decoration, headings, or illustration.

rules.name: The Lights Mean Something Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only as connection or result state. A colored dot that does not report state is a bug.

rules.name: The Neutral Hover Rule
rules.body: Hovering a resting card, row or nav item raises it with white opacity (border white 14%, fill white 5.5%), never with cyan. Cyan appears only once the element is active, selected, focused or a drop target.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a proportional sans for chrome. If text needs more emphasis, change size or color.

rules.name: The One Label Rule
rules.body: Every small uppercase label (section headers, eyebrows above titles, table column headers) uses the .section-title class: 11px, 0.22em tracking, Slate 400. No ad-hoc tracking values. Inside a destructive or warning context the label may take the state hue (text-red-200/80, text-amber-200/80), never cyan.

rules.name: The Flat Glass Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces get a border and a tonal step, not a drop shadow. Shadows belong to things that float above the workspace: menus, dialogs, the outer panel.

dos: Do use Signal Cyan only for the active, focused or primary element on a screen.
Do separate surfaces with a frost border (white 8–10%) and a white-opacity fill step.
Do keep the terminal on solid Terminal Ink, with no translucency behind text.
Do report connection state with the 8px status dot: green live, amber waiting, red failed.
Do match radius to surface size: 10px controls, 16px fields, ~22px cards, 28–32px panels.
donts: Don't add drop shadows to resting cards or rows; shadows are for floating layers.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or a non-monospace font for chrome.
Don't use colored dots, glows or tints that don't report state.
Don't use raw hex in components where an existing token or Tailwind class covers it.
Don't tint leading icon tiles, eyebrows, folder icons or hover states cyan; they stay neutral until active.
Don't put translucency behind the terminal: the terminal frame and its tab-bar column are solid `terminal-ink`.
